fitReason: Visitor-first, lower-physical-confidence methods backup. Current research directly concerns interactive RL, implicit human feedback, trust-aware adaptive autonomy and human-robot interaction. The 2026 TARS work adds trust signals to reward shaping; her author-hosted 2022 work explains behavior extraction, clustering and inverse RL for customized lane-change decisions. This is relevant to human-aware autonomy, although a current executed learned robot project is not verified.

physicalEvidence.summary: No learned physical robot execution is credited. The prior September 30 screen found the 2025 manufacturing-AGV study to use simulated/VR interactions. The September 2026 educational robot work involved curriculum and teaching activities rather than a demonstrated learned robot controller. The official 2025 NAVI project uses datasets, Unity mockups and scenario-driven simulation. The 2022 IRL study predicts lane-change actions from naturalistic driving data; collecting real vehicle data does not establish deployment of the learned controller. The 2026 TARS paper is supported by the author’s announcement and accessible abstract, but its full experimental methods were not retrieved, so platform, actual human-in-loop implementation and real-vehicle execution remain unverified.
